extracted.intended_audience: Researchers, principal investigators, and institutional grants administrators preparing NSF proposals and managing NSF awards
extracted.subtask_short: NSF proposal preparation and award compliance
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and mandatory policies for preparing and submitting proposals to the National Science Foundation and for award administration, compliance, reporting, and post‑award management. Covers proposal format, required proposal sections, merit review criteria, allowable costs, and grantee responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance with Instructions for Proposal Preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must conform with NSF proposal preparation and submission instructions including format, pagination, margins, and page formatting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes specific requirements for proposal format, pagination instructions, proposal margin and spacing requirements, and authorization procedures to deviate from NSF proposal preparation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Sections and Required Contents
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include specified sections (Cover Sheet, Project Summary, Table of Contents, Project Description, Results from Prior NSF Support (if applicable), References Cited, Biographical Sketches, Budget and Budget Justification, Current and Pending Support, Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources, Special Information and Supplementary Documentation, Appendices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each section has content expectations and may have page limits or formatting requirements; some program solicitations may modify general provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Description (including Page Limitations and URLs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Project Description must present the proposed work and adhere to page limits; inclusion of Uniform Resource Locators (URLs) within the Project Description is subject to restrictions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Project Description includes Results from Prior NSF Support when applicable; failure to follow page limits or include required content can affect review/acceptance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary
rubrics_metrics.description: A succinct summary section required in proposals to describe the project’s objectives and broader significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used by reviewers to understand the core elements of the proposed work; content expectations are specified in the PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Results from Prior NSF Support
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, proposals must include a section describing prior NSF support and the results achieved from that support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for renewals and proposals where prior NSF funding relates; reviewers use it to assess productivity and stewardship.

rubrics_metrics.name: References Cited
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include a References Cited section listing prior literature, data, and other sources referenced in the proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Standard bibliographic conventions apply; reviewers rely on references to evaluate context and novelty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch(es) Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Biographical sketches for senior personnel must include professional preparation, appointments, products, and synergistic activities (sections a–d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Format and content are specified; biosketches inform reviewers about investigator qualifications and prior contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include a detailed budget and budget justification covering salaries/wages, fringe benefits, equipment, travel, participant support, other direct costs, subawards, and indirect costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes policies on senior personnel salaries, administrative and clerical salaries, confidential budgetary information, and procedures for budget preparation and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salaries and Wages Policy (including Administrative and Clerical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies govern compensation for senior personnel and administrative/clerical salaries and wages and related procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific NSF policies on charging salaries (e.g., limitations on charging admin/clerical salaries to awards) and documentation requirements apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fringe Benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Fringe benefit costs must be budgeted and justified in accordance with institutional policies and applicable cost principles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Charged according to approved rates and documented in the budget justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel (General, Domestic, Foreign)
rubrics_metrics.description: Travel costs must be justified and categorized (general, domestic, foreign) in the budget and conform to NSF policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign travel has additional considerations; travel costs must be reasonable and necessary for project objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Participant Support Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: Participant support (e.g., stipends, travel, registration) must be identified and justified separately from other direct costs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participant support often has specific budgetary rules and affects indirect cost calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other Direct Costs (Materials, Publication/Dissemination, Consultants, Computer Services, Subawards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Other direct costs categories must be itemized and justified, including materials and supplies, publication/dissemination costs, consultant services, computer services, and subawards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subawards require additional documentation; consultant costs should follow NSF guidance on reasonableness and necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Costs (Facilities and Administrative Costs / F&A)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indirect costs must be calculated and requested according to institutional negotiated rates and NSF policy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF policy governs recovery of F&A costs and interactions with other cost principles; cognizant agency determinations may apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of This Request & Cost Sharing
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must state the amount of NSF funds requested and indicate any cost sharing (voluntary or mandatory) commitments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAPPG describes mandatory cost sharing situations, recordkeeping, and reporting requirements for cost sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable and Unallowable Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guide details which costs are allowable or unallowable under NSF awards (e.g., entertainment, meals and coffee breaks, alcoholic beverages typically unallowable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes basic considerations, conflicting guidelines, maximum obligation, pre‑award costs, post‑end costs, and requirements for prior written approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and Pending Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must disclose current and pending support for senior personnel, showing commitments of time and other funding sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to assess workload, overlap, and potential duplication of funding; omissions can affect eligibility and award decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities, Equipment and Other Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers must describe the institutional facilities, equipment, and other resources available to carry out the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate adequacy of resources to accomplish project aims; proposals lacking adequate resources may be disadvantaged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special Information and Supplementary Documentation / Appendices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on allowable supplementary documentation and appendices, and special processing instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendices are permitted only as specified; misuse (excessive or inappropriate appendices) can lead to page‑limit violations or review exclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: List of Suggested Reviewers or Reviewers Not to Include
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposers may submit names of suggested reviewers or reviewers not to include, per program instructions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF uses these lists as advisory only; conflicts of interest and selection criteria still govern reviewer selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proprietary or Privileged Information Handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for designating proprietary or privileged information in proposals and how NSF treats such material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation does not guarantee nondisclosure; legal and policy constraints apply to release of proposal information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Certifications and Required Forms
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must include required certifications (e.g., drug‑free workplace, debarment and suspension, lobbying, nondiscrimination) and standard forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certifications are mandatory; falsification or omission can affect awardability and lead to sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of Eligible Proposers (Who May Submit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines eligible proposer categories (IHEs, non‑profit, for‑profit organizations, state/local governments, unaffiliated individuals, international organizations, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special instructions apply to international branch campuses and other specific categories; eligibility affects submission route and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic Submission Requirements (DUNS, SAM, NSF ID)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals must meet electronic submission requirements, including DUNS/SAM registration and NSF ID where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to have required registrations can prevent submission or acceptance; follow Grants.gov or Research.gov/FastLane rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of Submissions and Proposal Mechanisms
rubrics_metrics.description: Describes submission types (letters of intent, preliminary proposals, full proposals) and special mechanisms (RAPID, EAGER, RAISE, GOALI, Ideas Lab, FASED, conference, equipment, center, infrastructure proposals).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each mechanism has tailored instructions and eligibility; check program solicitations for modifications to the PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Merit review will be guided by NSF's merit review principles as set forth in the PAPPG.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Principles inform reviewer behavior and evaluation approach; see Chapter III for detailed principles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the two NSF merit review criteria; assesses the potential to advance knowledge and understanding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate the quality, creativity, and potential impact of the proposed research; guidance and examples are provided in Chapter III.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit Review Criteria: Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the two NSF merit review criteria; assesses the potential to benefit society and contribute to desired societal outcomes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes education, outreach, broadening participation, societal benefits, and dissemination; proposers should describe plans to achieve broader impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of Reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF selects reviewers (program officers, ad hoc reviewers, panels) to evaluate proposals consistent with merit review principles and conflict of interest rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF may recruit subject matter experts and uses conflicts of interest guidance (Exhibit II‑2) when selecting reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proposal Processing, Review, Revisions and Funding Recommendation
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for proposal receipt, processing, review, revisions during review, and NSF's funding recommendation and decision framework (including risk management).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describes timeline and steps; includes NSF’s Risk Management Framework to inform award/decline decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification & Release of Review Information to PIs
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on what review information is provided to PIs and public release of grantee proposal information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs receive unattributed verbatim copies of peer reviews; some proposal and award information may be released per PAPPG policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award Instrument and NSF Award Conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines the award instrument (grant/cooperative agreement) and the award conditions that govern performance, reporting, and compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAPPG implements 2 CFR §200; when award conditions reference PAPPG sections, they become part of award requirements by incorporation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Periods, Start/End Dates, and No‑Cost Extensions
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing grant periods, start and end dates, and procedures for requesting no‑cost extensions or two‑year extensions for special creativity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests must follow PAPPG and any award conditions; certain extensions require prior approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Changes in Project Direction, Scope, or Key Personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must notify NSF and request approvals for changes in project direction, objectives, methods, PI/PD, co‑PI/co‑PD, or person‑months devoted to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant changes, delays, or changes in key personnel require prior NSF approval and may affect award terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subawarding / Transferring Part of an NSF Award (Subaward)
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies and procedures governing subawards, subcontracting, and the transfer of part of an NSF award to other entities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subawards require justification and oversight; the awardee retains responsibility for performance and compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postaward Addition of Postdoctoral Scholars
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for adding postdoctoral scholars to an award after award issuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow PAPPG rules for approvals, budget modifications, and reporting related to postdoc additions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical Reporting Requirements (Annual, Final, Project Outcomes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must submit annual project reports, a final project report, and a Project Outcomes Report for the general public as required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports must comply with content and submission timelines; noncompliance can affect future funding and closeout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for Financial Management and Payment Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must maintain financial management systems meeting NSF standards and follow payment, advance, and disbursement policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes requesting payments, working capital advances, banking information, handling erroneous payments, interest on advances, program income, and final disbursement reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record Retention, Audit, and Grant Closeout
rubrics_metrics.description: Requirements for record retention, audit cooperation, and procedures for grant closeout.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must retain records to support costs and compliance; audits and closeout reporting obligations are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grantee Standards: Conflict of Interest Policies
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must comply with conflict of interest policies to ensure objectivity in research and administration of NSF funds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutional COI policies and disclosure requirements apply; conflicts may affect eligibility to serve as reviewers or PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees have institutional responsibilities to promote and document training in the responsible conduct of research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF requires plans for RCR training and oversight; institutional responsibilities are described in the PAPPG.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property Management and Title to Equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies on property management standards, title to equipment (differing rules for non‑profit and for‑profit organizations), and conditions for acquisition and use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes accountability, recordkeeping, procedures when title is retained by NSF, and disposition at project end.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procurement Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Standards for procurement of goods and services under NSF awards, including competition, documentation, and allowable practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grantees must follow procurement rules that ensure fairness and reasonableness of costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowability of Costs: Direct Costs and Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines basic considerations for charging direct costs including compensation for personal services and allowable cost categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes rules on intra‑university consulting, federal employees, rearrangement and reconversion costs, and temporary dependent care travel costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indirect Cost Policy and Cognizant Agency Determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: NSF policy on indirect (F&A) costs and interaction with institutional cognizant agency determinations for negotiated rates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions must use negotiated indirect cost rates and provide supporting documentation when requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑Discrimination and Civil Rights Compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Grantees must comply with Title VI, Section 504, Title IX, Age Discrimination Act, E.O.11246, and Limited English Proficiency requirements under E.O.13166.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certification of compliance/civil rights certifications may be required; noncompliance can affect funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Living Organisms and Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects involving human subjects, vertebrate animals, recombinant or synthetic nucleic acid molecules, or DURC must comply with applicable protections and approvals (IRB, IACUC, IBC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protocols, approvals, and reporting requirements must be in place; absence of compliance can bar funding or trigger corrective actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government Permits, Activities Abroad, and International Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Projects involving activities abroad must obtain required permits and address passports/visas, charters, and host‑country regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional compliance and reporting obligations apply for foreign activities and collaborations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction, Davis‑Bacon Act, Bonding and Insurance, and Seismic Safety
rubrics_metrics.description: Construction or alteration projects must comply with construction‑specific statutes and standards (e.g., Davis‑Bacon prevailing wage requirements, bonding, insurance, seismic safety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: MREFC and large facility projects have additional processes and separate appropriations; accounting segregation required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intellectual Property, Patents, and Copyright
rubrics_metrics.description: Policies governing patents, inventions, copyrights, and dissemination of grant‑supported materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes grantee responsibilities, reporting of inventions, and special patent/copyright situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissemination and Sharing of Research Results
rubrics_metrics.description: Expectations for dissemination, sharing data and materials, publication/distribution of grant materials, and policies on costs and grantee obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NSF emphasizes sharing of results and may impose requirements for public access, repositories, and data management plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intergovernmental Review and Handling of Information
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures related to intergovernmental review of federal programs and handling/release of information collected under grants (e.g., questionnaires, data release).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow applicable statutes and PAPPG guidance on confidential information and public release.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grant Administration Disputes, Suspension, Termination, and Research Misconduct
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedures for informal resolution, suspension, termination, and review procedures, and policies for reporting and handling research misconduct.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes definitions, rights of parties, reporting obligations, and OIG oversight; grantees must report possible misconduct and cooperate with investigations.
